newsitem.title: FRANCE: CrLocal de France 96 lending rose 14 pct.
newsitem.headline: CrLocal de France 96 lending rose 14 pct.

text.p: French bank Credit Local de France (CLF), which has allied with Credit Communal de Belgique under the Dexia name, said on Thursday that lending in 1996 rose 14 percent from 1995 to 28 billion francs.
"The merger of Credit Local de France and Credit Communal de Belgique is the most important event for Credit Local de France since it was created in 1987," it said.

"Dexia will make it possible to optimise the allocation of group assets and to improve structurally the return on equity, which should rise in the next few years from 11 percent to 13 percent," it said.
The lending rise of 14 percent was on a comparable basis, excluding German subsidiary CLF-Hypothekenbank Berlin, which reported loans of 28 billion francs, it said.

"Although growth in Europe was weak in 1996, Credit Local de France/Dexia Group will have been one of the few financial institutions to report a significant increase in both new commitments and outstanding loans," Pierre Richard, chairman of Credit Local de France and Dexia Group said in the statement.
"Outstanding loans rose from 366 billion francs in 1995 to more than 407 billion in 1996, for an increase of 11 percent," it said.
In the French public sector, new commitments including the acquisition of external loans rose 11 percent to 43.3 billion francs, it said, and the group maintained its market share of 40-45 percent.
At an operational level, the group said it planned to share work procedures with Credit Communal de Belgique in the area of lending to local governments to increase the unit size of commitments.
Internationally, it said "lending took a giant leap forward" once the addition of loans made in Germany on a full-year basis was taken into account. (( -- Paris Newsroom +33 1 4221 5452))
